More recirculation always improves treatment without limit
The influent load tripled during the maximum rate week
The filter media failed during the maximum rate week only

inference.explanation: Load is unchanged and media did not fail for one week only. The plant record showing best performance at a moderate rate contradicts an unlimited benefit claim. Short contact at maximum rate supports an optimum rate explanation.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Recirculation rate and effluent quality comparison record for the test weeks
Chlorine log
Digester log

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Effluent was best at the moderate rate and worse at maximum, at unchanged load, across the test weeks.
clueText.nc-b: Chlorine records do not test recirculation.
clueText.nc-c: Digester records do not test filter contact time.

tasks.prompt: A waste activated sludge line plugs repeatedly at the same elbow during cold weather.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated shift unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: Plugs occur at an exposed outdoor elbow on nights below minus 20 C.
The line runs at low velocity overnight when wasting is paused, letting sludge sit in the exposed section.
Flushing the line before the night pause on trial prevented plugs through the next cold week.
Waste pump pressure and sludge solids are normal.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Sludge sitting and freezing or thickening in the exposed low point during night pauses is plugging the waste line in cold weather
The waste pump is too weak for the sludge at all times
The elbow is undersized and plugs in all seasons
The sludge solids have doubled permanently

inference.explanation: Pump pressure and solids are normal and plugs are seasonal and location specific, so weak pump, doubled solids, and all season undersizing are contradicted. Sitting sludge in an exposed elbow plus prevention by flushing supports cold stagnation plugging.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Effluent pH log
Chlorine log
Waste line plug location and temperature record with the flushing trial note

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Effluent ph does not test waste line plugging.
clueText.nc-b: Chlorine records do not test sludge line freezing.
clueText.nc-c: No plugs occurred in the trial cold week when the line was flushed before each night pause.

tasks.prompt: Operators notice the aeration tank smells sour and effluent quality falls after a long weekend with no operator visits at a small plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated shift unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: The blower was found tripped off on arrival Monday, with its breaker tripped at some point over the weekend.
Dissolved oxygen is zero and the mixed liquor smells sour on Monday morning.
Restarting the blower and restoring oxygen brings effluent quality back over two days.
Influent load over the weekend was normal low small town flow.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The clarifier failed over the weekend and caused the sour tank
Operators visiting causes treatment to work by itself
A blower outage over the unvisited weekend left the tank without oxygen, so treatment stalled and the liquor went sour until air was restored
Weekend influent is toxic in this town every week

inference.explanation: No weekly toxic pattern is recorded, and visits alone do not treat waste, the running equipment does. Clarifier failure would not zero the tank oxygen or sour the liquor. A tripped blower with zero oxygen and recovery on restart supports the outage explanation.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Chlorine log
Grit log
Blower trip record and Monday oxygen and effluent recovery log

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Chlorine records do not test weekend aeration.
clueText.nc-b: Grit records do not test blower outages.
clueText.nc-c: Oxygen and effluent recovered over two days after the blower restart, at normal weekend load.

tasks.prompt: A primary clarifier in a combined sewer town carries over solids during spring rain events, then performs normally in dry weather.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated shift unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: Rain event flows reach three times the dry weather average at this combined sewer plant.
Surface overflow rate during rain calculates well above the design value.
Dry weather effluent quality, blanket, and draw off are all normal.
An upstream storage tank trial that shaved the rain peak improved clarifier performance in the next rain event.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Rain dilutes sewage so carryover should be impossible and the results are errors
The clarifier scraper fails only when it rains
Rain driven hydraulic overload in the combined system is washing solids through the clarifier during events
A toxic rain contaminant stops settling during events

inference.explanation: A scraper that fails only in rain is unsupported, and dilution does not prevent hydraulic washout at three times flow, as the overflow rate shows. No toxic contaminant is recorded. Peak shaving improving performance supports hydraulic overload.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Rain flow, overflow rate, and storage trial record for spring events
Digester log
Blower log

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Carryover tracked rain flow peaks and eased in the event where storage shaved the peak.
clueText.nc-b: Digester records do not test rain hydraulics.
clueText.nc-c: Blower records do not test primary washout.

tasks.prompt: Effluent disinfection by chlorine works in summer but a winter survey shows much longer contact is needed at low temperature for the same kill in bench tests.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated shift unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: Bench tests at 4 C need about twice the contact time of tests at 20 C for the same bacteria reduction, at the same residual.
Winter effluent bacteria results are marginal at the summer contact tank setting.
Residual, flow, and tank baffling are unchanged between seasons.
Increasing winter contact by using the full tank volume on trial improved winter bacteria results.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Winter bacteria are a different species that chlorine cannot kill
Chlorine loses all disinfecting power at 4 C
The contact tank shrinks in winter and holds less volume
Cold water slowing chlorine disinfection is making the summer contact setting marginal in winter

inference.explanation: Chlorine still works in cold bench tests, it just needs longer, so total power loss is contradicted. No species change is recorded, and the tank volume is fixed. Slower cold disinfection in paired bench tests plus improvement with full volume supports the temperature effect.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Paired temperature bench disinfection record and winter contact trial note
Screenings log
Grit log

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Bench kill at 4 C matched summer kill when contact time was about doubled.
clueText.nc-b: Screenings records do not test contact time.
clueText.nc-c: Grit records do not test disinfection kinetics.

tasks.prompt: A small plant operator finds the effluent weir of the secondary clarifier coated in green growth and effluent solids slightly elevated.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated shift unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: The growth is green algae on sunlit weir surfaces, thickest on the south facing side.
Scraping the weirs on trial lowered effluent solids measured the same week.
Settleability, blanket, and return rate are all normal.
Effluent solids elevation is small and mostly in afternoon samples on sunny days.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Algae growing on the sunlit effluent weirs is sloughing into the effluent and raising afternoon solids slightly
The clarifier is hydraulically overloaded every sunny afternoon
Algae cannot grow on weirs, so the growth must be sludge
Filamentous bulking is raising effluent solids

inference.explanation: Settleability and hydraulics are normal, so bulking and overload are unsupported. Algae do grow on sunlit wet surfaces, and the south facing, sunny afternoon, scraping response pattern supports weir algae sloughing.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Digester log
Weir growth inspection and scraping trial with afternoon sample record
Influent flow log

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Digester records do not test weir growth.
clueText.nc-b: Afternoon solids fell in the week after weir scraping, at unchanged process settings.
clueText.nc-c: Flow records do not test algae sloughing.

tasks.prompt: Sludge volume index is calculated very high one day, but the settleability cylinder and clarifier both look normal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater plant case. Readings are from the stated shift unless a bench or paired check is noted. Archived plant records are available for follow up.

evidence.label: The mixed liquor suspended solids result used in the calculation came back at half its usual value from the lab.
A retained sample reanalysed reads at the usual mixed liquor value, which returns the index to the normal range.
The settled volume in the cylinder was at its usual value.
Clarifier blanket and effluent clarity are normal all day.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: True bulking occurred for one calculation and vanished
The cylinder test is wrong and the index is right
A low mixed liquor lab result in error inflated the calculated index, while actual settleability stayed normal
Operators misread the settled volume by half

inference.explanation: Settled volume and clarifier behaviour are normal, and the retained sample reanalysis restores the index, so true one day bulking is contradicted. No cylinder or reading error is recorded. The erroneous low solids result explains the inflated index.

nextClue.prompt: Which next check best distinguishes the supported explanation from the alternatives?

options.label: Grit log
Retained sample reanalysis and index recalculation record for the day
Chlorine log

nextClue.explanation: This check tests the supported explanation directly against the alternatives. The other choices do not isolate the cause shown by the evidence.

clueText.nc-a: Grit records do not test mixed liquor results.
clueText.nc-b: Recalculating with the reanalysed solids value returns the index to the normal plant range.
clueText.nc-c: Chlorine records do not test index calculations.
